listening.q: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
o: A report that needs to be completed
listening.e: They discuss checking the figures and submitting the report before the deadline.

listening.q: What does the man still need to do?
listening.e: He says he still needs to check the figures in the final section.

listening.q: When does the professor want to receive the report?
listening.e: The woman says the professor wants it before noon tomorrow.

swo.q: The committee _____ the final decision yesterday.
swo.e: The time expression 'yesterday' requires the simple past: made.

swo.q: The new library, _____ last year, is already popular with students.
swo.e: The past participle 'completed' works as a reduced passive adjective clause.

swo.q: Neither the students nor the teacher _____ aware of the schedule change.
swo.e: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Teacher' is singular, so use was.

swo.q: The researcher collected the data carefully, _____ the results were reliable.
swo.e: 'So' introduces the result: careful collection led to reliable results.

reading.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Why cities should remove old trees
The benefits of urban trees and the need for careful planning
Why all tree species grow well on sidewalks
reading.e: The passage describes several benefits and explains why tree selection and maintenance matter.

reading.q: According to the passage, how can trees help manage rainwater?
o: By intercepting water and improving soil absorption
reading.e: The passage states that leaves intercept some water and roots can improve soil absorption.

reading.q: The word 'intercepted' is closest in meaning to _____.
reading.e: In context, leaves catch or hold some of the rainwater.

reading.q: Why might a tree be unsuitable for a narrow sidewalk?
o: It may attract too many birds
Its roots may damage pavement or pipes
reading.e: The passage specifically mentions possible damage from roots.

audio.title: Sample conversation (browser voice)
audio.script: Woman: Have you finished the report for Professor Allen? Man: Almost. I still need to check the figures in the final section. Woman: The professor said he would like to receive it before noon tomorrow. Man: That should be fine. I will review it tonight and send it first thing in the morning. Woman: Great. Let me know if you need me to check anything.

reading.title: Urban Trees and City Life
reading.passage: Urban trees provide benefits that extend beyond their appearance. Their leaves can provide shade, reducing the amount of heat absorbed by streets and buildings. Trees also help manage rainwater: some water is intercepted by leaves, while roots can improve the soil's ability to absorb rainfall. In addition, urban vegetation creates habitats for birds and insects. However, planting trees in cities requires careful planning. Species must be selected according to local climate, available space, and maintenance needs. A tree that grows well in a park may not be suitable for a narrow sidewalk where roots could damage pavement or underground pipes. Therefore, successful urban forestry depends not simply on planting more trees, but on choosing appropriate species and caring for them over time.
